1	To better understand what SilverBullet is doing, especially when [[Troubleshooting]], it is good to know where and how to look at SilverBullet logs.
2	
3	Start with [[Workbench/Console]] for the combined Lua, JavaScript, plug and service-worker log. For lower-level diagnostics, open your browser’s JavaScript console.
4	
5	* Client logs: Check your browser’s JavaScript console. Usually these are part of “(Web) Developer Tools” buried somewhere in a Tools or Developer menu.
6	* Service worker logs (especially useful when debugging [[Sync]] issues):
7	  * In Chromium-based browsers these logs are mixed with the regular JavaScript console.
8	  * In Firefox start at `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` then find it under the Service Worker section and click “Inspect”.
9	  * In Safari they can be accessed via `Developer > Service workers`.
10	* Server logs: Server logs are written to the standard output of the server process.
11	* Reverse proxy logs: if you use some sort of reverse proxy, check those as well. Reverse proxies may do some surprising stuff, like block certain requests.
